title: Data Depths
description: Sharding, queues and surviving traffic spikes.

options: Copying all data to several read-only replicas
Splitting the rows across several databases, each owning a slice
challenges.explanation: Each shard holds part of the data, so writes spread out too. Replicas copy everything and only help with reads.

challenges.prompt: For a global social app, which shard key is most likely to create a hot shard?
challenges.explanation: Countries are wildly uneven: one shard would get a huge share of the users. Hashing a high-cardinality ID spreads load evenly.

challenges.prompt: Why use consistent hashing instead of shard = hash(key) % N?
options: Adding or removing a shard moves only about 1/N of the keys instead of almost all of them
It removes the need for replicas
challenges.explanation: With modulo, changing N remaps nearly every key. On a hash ring, a new node only takes over the keys between it and its neighbor.

challenges.prompt: An analytics service ingests events: 70% of requests are writes. Caches and replicas will not save you here.
challenges.explanation: 3,500 writes/s need at least 4 shards (1,000 writes/s each). Replicas and caches only help reads. A queue can turn slow synchronous writes into fast acknowledgements.

challenges.prompt: Orders spike 3× for ten minutes during a sale. How does a message queue help?
options: It buffers the burst, so workers process orders at a steady rate
challenges.explanation: The queue absorbs the spike and workers drain it at the database's pace. Users get a quick acknowledgement instead of a timeout.

challenges.prompt: Your queue delivers each message at least once. Why must the payment worker be idempotent?
options: A retried message must not charge the customer twice
challenges.explanation: At-least-once means duplicates happen. Use an idempotency key (like the order ID) and skip work that is already done.

challenges.prompt: Which rate-limiting algorithm allows short bursts while keeping the long-term average under control?
challenges.explanation: Tokens refill at a steady rate and can pile up to the bucket size, so a client can burst briefly but not exceed the average for long.

challenges.prompt: Black Friday: traffic hits 3× the normal 4,000 req/s, and 40% of requests are orders. Survive the spike.
challenges.explanation: At peak, 4,800 writes/s would need 5 shards. A queue lets the database absorb them at the average rate (1,600/s), so 2 shards are enough. A cache handles the reads.
